review_text: I've been a wet shaver (safety razor, soap, and brush) for many years, but decided to try an electric to save time in the morning. I bought some Williams Lectric Shave and researched electric shaving technique online. After being disappointed by a foil, I settled on the 7180XL. It's a good mid-level razor at a reasonable price, balancing quietness, speed, ergonomics, and the necessary features. Unfortunately, it was too much of a step down from a proper wet shave. I didn't like: - the lack of precision (three cutting disks on a planar surface the size of my cheek) - it missed a lot of hairs, requiring several passes for a clean shave - although I used a light touch, pushing the shaver through the stubble was still irritating - the shave was socially acceptable in appearance, but rough to the touch - I had a 5 o'clock shadow by 2 o'clock - you can't do a close multi-pass shave for special occasions like you can with a blade - I started getting ingrown hairs on my neck Regarding the last point above, you really can't address that by using a blade on just special occasions. The face needs time to adjust to a change in shaving method, so if you switch between methods neither will be optimal. The 7180XL is a perfectly good razor for men who are satisfied with a socially acceptable shave and whose face can tolerate the rotary shaving system. It just wasn't my cup of tea. I now wet shave at night and still have less of a shadow by 5 o'clock than I would using an electric shaver in the morning.

review_text: I was due for a new razor and asked my wife for one as a Christmas gift. She purchased the Norelco7180XL at Sears for about $85.00 thinking it was a good quality razor, which it is. (Still made in Holland as another reviewer wrote). It looked great, and I was excited about the water clean up feature. After an overnight charge, I gave it a test run. It was remarkably light and very quiet, it almost seemed to be running too slow to actually work, but it did a good job of removing my stubble. Just one problem - It seemed to really abrade my face, which was quite irritated afterwards. I do have sensitive skin, which is why I don't use a standard razor, but I never had this problem with the Braun, or the Remington razors I owned previously. It states in the users manual that it may take a few weeks to get used to Norelco's patented lift & cut system, but I don't think I would ever get used to the irritation this razor caused. Call me a pansy, but I had to return the razor, and am now in search of a new Braun model with better ergonomics, and a smooth, painless shave. Just wanted to submit this review as a heads up to anyone else who is contemplating this razor, and has sensitive skin.

review_text: As it turns out I live only 20 miles from West Coast Shaving. I called them and said I would drop in. A new boar brush must be broken in which takes a couple of weeks because the tips of the bristles seem too firm and rather sharp when it's first used. My observation is that not only does the lanolin soften up your skin nicely but it has helped brake in the boar bruch very quickly. The lanolin seems to soften up the brush just like it softens up your beard. This only took about three shaves and my boar brush is perfect. I read all the reviews and saw the videos on this soap. I didn't find any problems with the soap as far a lathering. I soaked it in WARM water and took my boar brush to start to lather it up. No problem. I didn't find all the problems that other people talk about. This might be the results of the water hardness rather than the soap itself.

review_text: Purchased this product directly from Revel rather than going through Amazon. Although my shipment was delayed due to an error on their end, customer support was so helpful! Huge thank you to Danielle at Revel Nails who helped this gift arrive in time for Christmas! I ordered Margo (a pretty warm pale pink with lots of irridencent microglitter), Euphoric (a non-shimmery light blue) and my favorite color, Julia ( a sheer light pink with lots of iridescent microglitter). Application is easy, but getting a smooth finish definitely takes attention to detail. It really is worth taking extra time to file down the powder before applying the finishing gel - this makes the product thinner on the nail and feel more natural and less lumpy. My soon-to-be sister in law and I played around with applying the colors, and managed to do both hands in around 1/2 hour. I also did a test to make sure it removed easily. Within 24 hours I was excited to put on a new set! So so so happy with the finished result of the product, and would definitely recommend to friends.

review_text: I have had these long enough to test all three colors. I'm satisfied these are clearly NOT frost. If you apply correctly, the mirror effect is better than the powders. However, the gold is more of a gold/green, not a true gold. The silver & rose gold are beautiful. To apply correctly and have the mirror effect, you must adhere to nail tech guidelines!! 1. Wash & scrub your nails with a nail brush. 2. Dry your nails! 3. Apply a base coat. This is VERY important to have a filled in base on your nails. I use Mia's. 4. Apply one thin coat to each nail. 5. Use a nail corrector pen or small brush dipped in acetone to remove any on cuticles. 6. Go back to first nail painted and apply a second, thicker coat. Repeat on other nails. 7. Repeat step 5. 8. Apply your choice of top coat. I use Mia's in my salon. If you can't get the same results, you're either not putting a base and top coat on or you're using too much on your first coat. Enjoy!!

review_text: I bought this because I was wanting to try fiberglass without spending a ton on something I might hate. I definitely do not hate these nails! They are thin and natural looking, and still super strong. I will absolutely continue using fiberglass nails. BUT... They are a bit of a pain to use, and some of that pain is actual, physical pain from getting fiberglass stuck in your skin. I'd advise using gloves, and will follow my own advice on that going forward. Fiberglass is actual wee little glass fibers which are nearly impossible to see and remove when you get a bit stuck in your skin and can be really irritating and painful. I ended up smearing my hands with tacky glue, letting it dry, and then peeling it off to get rid of the it. It worked pretty well, but yeah, gloves. The gel in this set cured well, and as I said, my nails are very strong. I used Young Nails Protien Bond and the base coat, and so far no lifting whatsoever, when I usually would start seeing some. The little LED light is cute, but I wouldn't ever use it for curing nails. I have a better light and I halved the recommending curing times since they're given for the tiny lamp. There's a little tin of loose fibers, which I'm not sure how to use. The set also comes with two completely useless pairs of tweezers, which I just tossed.

review_text: I’ve never heard of this brand, but my wife loves to try new moisturizers and face creams. This one contains green tea, retinol, collagen, hyaluronic acid, and MSM. Who knows how much of each is in here compared to other products like it, but my wife likes it. The jar has a top that you push down lightly to dispense. You swipe that off with your fingers, so you don’t actually open the jar (unless you want to). She doesn’t really like the top, though, because if you’re not careful, too much comes out. Also, there is no pickup tube that goes to the bottom, so you have to keep whacking the top against your hand, as if you’re packing a new box of smokes, or it’ll run dry. There is no smell, or at least neither one of us could smell anything at all. It’s very creamy (white), and absorbs into her skin quickly. There is a moist, tacky feeling to the skin for a few minutes, and then it’s gone. So you have to wait a few minutes after application to apply makeup. She has pretty sensitive skin, and said there was no redness or tightness, or any adverse reaction at all. Too early to tell if it reduces wrinkles, but as far as anti-aging goes, she wore this cream for about a week, and her birthday still came. Hope this helps.

review_text: First let me say: READ my review CAREFULLY to avoid an eyebrow malfunction like I experienced. Second, the tint works great!! Third, I’m grateful for the bike chain degreaser I still had hibernating in my cupboard, 20 years later. Read on: I tinted my eyebrows thinking that it was OK to get some on the skin above and below my eyebrows and that it would wash off easily. After all, when I self-color my hair, the excess color wipes off my skin with no problem!! Ya, nope not true of this eyebrow tint. The excess wouldn’t come off!!! In hindsight, I had a very Low IQ moment. The instructions do tell you to test a patch of your skin before using it on your eyebrows. I didn’t do that. You should!! After I washed the tint off and attempted to wash the excess tint off, I saw a female Groucho Marx in the mirror. I tried removing the excess tint with 3 different face soaps, then regular body wash soap, then baking soda, then toothpaste. Tier 2: Shout with bleach, Comet spray w/bleach. Then Lysol wipes... moved onto nail polish remover. Then hairspray. But what actually did it was the 🚲 bike degreaser I use on my bike chain. Thank goodness because I was about ready to just dump an entire Costco-sized bottle of bleach on my face and let a higher power step in!! Worth noting: it was an eyebrow tint product from Slovenia so it probably doesn’t have the same ease of removal standards as American hair color products! Great product but just be very careful not to overdo it and don’t get it on the skin near your eyebrows!! Aim carefully at JUST your eyebrows!! PS. I am sparing you a picture of my mishap...you’re welcome!! 😊🤣

review_text: This product actually does whiten teeth. If it doesn't - you haven't been to a dentist in a while! I see a few people complain that it doesn't work, but you have to consider....It took quite a while for your teeth to get discolored - months, or even years. You can't expect anything ( even dentist whitening) to whiten your teeth over night. A dentist whitening has you come back several times - depending on how white you want. It will take weeks, even months using this to get your teeth close to white, but if you use this every day - you will see a difference. One more thing - instructions tell you to wet the tooth brush and dab it in the powder. What they do not instruct is if the powder in the container gets wet - mold will begin to grow on it. This happened with my first order. Now, I put a small amount of powder on the outside top of the lid, dab with a wet brush, then throw the small amount left away. You can gauge the amount of powder needed for one use, so you don't waste too much.

review_text: Purchased on a whim, to see if it would do what other products promised and didn't completely deliver. It does deliver. I have an old parquet floor that has aged and faded from before I bought my house. Other products advertised themselves as restorers for this kind of problem. They did after a fashion but still left the floor looking mostly the way it was before. Given my experience with the other products, I didn't have great hopes for this product, but to my surprise, just one application of this beeswax product has pretty much done the trick. The fading is pretty much gone and the wood has a warm, lustrous look now. It also brought back the original finish on some items of furniture I tried it on, simply wiping it on the wood. Instructions are minimal, so use caution with the sponge: it absorbs the wax, so there is a reserve of wax inside it. When I went to rinse off the dust from the sponge I squeezed it and wax came out with every squeeze. The sponge is large and the bottle is small, so getting the right amount of wax on the sponge takes some practice. Remember: a little goes a long way and the sponge absorbs the wax, so after a while use that instead of continuously reapplying new wax. A wonderful product.

review_text: I buy a lot from Amazon but write few reviews. I have to be either delighted or very disappointed to be motivated. In this case, sadly, it’s the latter. Please note that it applies specifically to one print: “Psychedelic” For the price you can get a dozen or two in solid colors from other vendors, as I have done. But I was quite attracted to the supposedly “bright psychedelic print”. When it arrived just now I was terribly disappointed. They’re basically pastel, and I don’t do pastels. I might keep them as a gift simply because returns are such a hassle. As far as the idea of these types of hair ties, so far so good. They do seem to hurt less and as I’m prone to migraines that’s a big plus. But they also stretch out after a few uses, but can be rehabilitated. Having bought a big lot inexpensively, I’ll just work my way through them then throw them in a pot of hot water to shrink up again. (The big batch I bought had instructions for shrinking: hit with a hair dryer or hot water. For a batch, the latter seems easier. As long as I only need to do that every few weeks, that’s fine.) Good luck!! Ohhhh: One more note: If you’re wondering why these are so much more expensive than other ties made from “telephone cord,” it seems to be advertising and presentation. That I learned about them through Teleties advertising might make me keep them. But I really didn’t need them to arrive in a solid gold-foil bubble padded envelope (which I didn’t even know existed!) Just in case you wonder where your money is going....

review_text: Like most reviewers, the prospect of 12 lip liners was too tempting to pass up. I use soft crayon liners, or a brush of my lipstick, to create an one-the-spot liner all the time - so this seemed like a great buy. These are clearly imported. The good news is the manufacturer actually lists the ingredients on the box; I've taken a photo of the box so you can see the ingredients - personally, I don't recommend using products where you can't see the ingredients before you order. The pencils you get are an interesting range, and seem to vary from package to package. Mine were in a variety of colors; the one color I was looking for - a basic nude - was not in my package - but I got a range of plums (which I never wear) and pinks (which I rarely wear). If you've used any of your mom's pencils, you're familiar with carmine, which can flake. You have to be careful with the pressure used to avoid application debris, but it's the best to stop lipstick from bleeding or feathering. Since none of the colors were perfect, I used a lighter pink with my lipstick so it wasn't noticeable, and it worked fine.

All in all for $20, I would definitely recommend.

review_text: I really like using this oil, it has a peppery smell and it absorbs into the skin really nice. I love that it is organic and how it makes my winter skin feel all moisturized and lush!! I also have naturally curly hair and my curls look pretty for a change, not all glued together like some products, or dried out and blah like others!
